correctness.rationale: All quantifiers and boundary dimensions were reconstructed. In dimension one, orthogonal invariance and the valuation identity determine the two intrinsic-volume coefficients. For \\(d\\ge2\\), Lotz's verified Theorem 1.1 gives the unique intrinsic-volume representation. Evaluating on subspaces and decomposing a k-plane as k full one-dimensional factors times d-k zero factors forces \\(a_{d,k}=(d-k)\\alpha+k\\beta\\). Normalization of intrinsic volumes yields \\(\\mu_d=\\alpha d+(\\beta-\\alpha)\\delta\\). The converse follows from the nondecreasing coefficient criterion and the verified intrinsic-volume convolution. No finite experiment substitutes for the all-dimensional proof.

originality.rationale: The primary 2026 theorem gives a separate nondecreasing coefficient vector in each dimension but no compatibility across Cartesian products. The older canonicality theorem for statistical dimension assumes its values on every linear subspace (and localizability), whereas the present claim assumes only product additivity and two one-dimensional anchors, from which all subspace values are derived. Targeted published-finding corpus and web searches found no equivalent cross-dimensional two-parameter classification. The residual risk is a differently phrased monoidal result in older valuation literature.
residual_risks: The literature search was targeted rather than exhaustive; an older valuation-theory source could encode the same cross-dimensional product classification under different monoidal terminology.
The theorem relies on the correctness of the recent fixed-dimensional classification arXiv:2609.09335; that theorem was inspected but not reproved here.

value.rationale: Cartesian-product compatibility is a natural structural requirement because conic intrinsic-volume distributions convolve under products and statistical dimension is additive. The result collapses the newly classified (d+1)-parameter cone in each dimension to one universal two-parameter family across all dimensions, and the normalized form derives every subspace calibration from only two one-dimensional anchors. This is a motivated structural rigidity statement rather than a renamed special case or a numerical recomputation; it isolates exactly why statistical dimension is the unique normalized monoidal member of the monotone invariant valuation class.
